table.step: Setup (definitions, settings, starting state, input table)
table.ruleA: 6 tiers numbered 1 to 6. Budget/heat/cool = 10/7/3, 8/6/2, 12/9/4, 6/5/2, 9/7/3, 7/5/2. Start 3,6,6,2,2,1, all COLD. Stack limit 38. Drop count 0. All divisions round down. Ingest schedule rows 0 6 3 5 3 3 / 4 2 0 1 1 7 / 4 4 3 0 0 6 / 7 6 7 1 3 0 / 0 6 6 3 3 0.
table.ruleB: 6 compartments numbered 1 to 6. Volume/inception/desinence identical to A's values. Start 3,6,6,2,2,1, all LAMINAR. Blow limit 38. Total Overboard 0. Quarters and halves round down. Fill Table identical to A's schedule.

table.ruleA: Add this cycle's schedule entry to each tier. Budget is not enforced.
table.ruleB: Add this cycle's fill amount to each compartment. Volume is not enforced.

table.ruleA: Go in order 1 to 6, one tier at a time. If count > budget (strictly), the excess goes to tier n+1 and the tier is set to its budget. The excess arrives before the next tier is handled, so overflow cascades. Excess from tier 6 is added to the drop count.
table.ruleB: Go in order 1 to 6, one compartment at a time. If contents > volume (strictly), the excess goes aft to n+1 and the compartment is set to its volume. It arrives before the next one is checked, so overflow cascades. Excess from compartment 6 goes overboard.

table.ruleA: Read counts after step 2. A COLD tier at or above its heat mark (>=) becomes HOT. A HOT tier at or below its cool mark (<=) becomes COLD. Otherwise the state is kept. At most one change per cycle. Log each change as (cycle, tier, before, after).
table.ruleB: Read contents after step 2. A LAMINAR pump at or above its inception mark (>=) becomes CAVITATING. A CAVITATING pump at or below its desinence mark (<=) becomes LAMINAR. Otherwise the state is kept. At most one change per cycle. Log each change the same way.

table.ruleA: Use counts at the start of the step and states after step 3. Amount is floor(count/4) for COLD and floor(count/2) for HOT. All six amounts are computed first, then applied at once: each tier loses its own amount. A COLD amount is dropped. A HOT amount goes to tier n-1, or is dropped from tier 1. Budget is not enforced.
table.ruleB: Use contents at the start of the step and states after step 3. Amount is floor(contents/4) for LAMINAR and floor(contents/2) for CAVITATING. All six are computed first, then applied together: each compartment loses its amount. A LAMINAR amount goes overboard. A CAVITATING amount backflows to n-1, or goes overboard from compartment 1. Volume is not enforced.

table.ruleA: Fires if the total of all six counts after step 4 is > 38 strictly (38 does not fire). When it fires, ONLY HOT tiers are halved (floor) and COLD tiers are left unchanged. The removed chunks are dropped, and the cycle is logged.
table.ruleB: Fires if the total of all six contents after step 4 is > 38 strictly (38 does not fire). When it fires, EVERY compartment is halved (floor), whatever its pump state. The removed water goes overboard, and the cycle is logged.
table.difference: The trigger, its strictness, the timing and where the removed amount goes all match. The positions halved differ: A halves only HOT tiers, B halves all six. A COLD/LAMINAR position holding 2 or more units when the halving fires keeps all of them under A but loses floor-half under B. That changes later quantities, loss, states and halving cycles.

table.ruleA: (a) end counts 1 to 6, (b) end states, (c) state changes in order, (d) reset cycles, (e) final drop count, (f) balance check.
table.ruleB: (a) end contents 1 to 6, (b) end pump states, (c) pump state changes, (d) emergency blow cycles or none, (e) Total Overboard, (f) balance check.

result.probeWhy: The only suspected difference is which positions the line-wide halving applies to. So the probe has to fire the halving while a COLD/LAMINAR position holds 2 or more units. On the printed tables both halvings (cycles 1 and 4) find every position with 2 or more units already HOT: in cycle 1 only tier 1 (3) and tier 6 (1) are COLD, and floor(1/2)=0, which leaves tier 1. So the printed run hides the difference. The first probe I tried (all 9s, no input) also missed it, because every position went HOT, and a second hand-made probe never fired the halving. This probe was picked by a script search to differ in every report field. Hand check of cycle 1: after fill [9,11,2,9,14,9], the overflow cascades to [9,8,5,6,9,7] with 10 dropped. Position 3 (5 < 9) stays COLD and the rest go HOT. After pumping the totals are [9,4,7,7,8,4] = 39 > 38, so the halving fires. A leaves position 3 at 7. B halves it to 3, losing 4 more. In cycle 2, position 3 reaches 11 under A (goes HOT) but only 7 under B (stays LAMINAR), and the runs diverge from there.
result.differingRule: In step 5, A halves only the HOT tiers and leaves COLD tiers alone, while B halves every compartment whatever its pump state. Every other rule matches, including the trigger (total > 38, strictly) and where the removed amount goes.
result.trust:
The two routes agree. The table found the difference by reading the documents, and the probe confirmed it. The printed tables give identical reports from A and B, because the only COLD tiers at each halving hold 0 or 1 chunk, or 3 in tier 1 during cycle 1. So the printed tables alone would wrongly suggest SAME.

The arithmetic was done with a Python script, C:\Users\Jaket\AppData\Local\Temp\om\desk-fm\P16\p16_routes_claude.py. I checked cycle 1 of the probe by hand. Both routes balance on every run: 114=114 on the printed tables, 109=109 on the probe. A random check of 20,000 cases gave identical A and B reports in 15,396 of them, so the difference shows only when the halving fires while a COLD position holds 2 or more units.
